pairs.subject: media-playback
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/CutClock.tsx:246 The cut/score transport writes the playhead into React state on every animation frame, so the whole Cut and Score editors (Monitor, every CutClock lane and block, the timecode) re-render at frame rate for the length of playback. This is the ancestral defect playback-clock exists to prevent, even though the hook's own comment says it is 'outside React's render'.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/CutClock.tsx:246 The playhead lives in useState and is set every rAF tick. The mutable ref `at` exists, but the needle and readout are not fed by a narrow frame-loop consumer or a throttled subscription. The wall-clock-delta advance on line 243 is correct.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Cut.tsx:63 The Monitor finds the piece on screen from the clock and each scene's interval, with no chaining, so seek is a pure function of the derived timeline. The scan is linear rather than sorted, which is fine at about 30 scenes.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/CutClock.tsx:250 The frame loop names its reaper on pause, on rate change and on unmount. The Render preview loop also cancels (Render.tsx:61).

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Cut.tsx:119 The cut clock drives still plates with no engine to await. The only audible engines are stock <audio controls> elements, which the platform's own controls cover.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Takes.tsx:238 Takes play only through platform media elements with stock behaviour. No second engine shares one contract.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Cut.tsx:71 Content is made ahead of time by kernel jobs and read from the blob store. Nothing is produced just ahead of the playhead.

pairs.subject: media-playback
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/audio/_audio/useTransport.ts:89 A card's play control flips to 'playing' the moment it is pressed, before the element answers, and nothing listens for 'waiting' or 'stalled'. A slow or buffering take is drawn as playing until the 'playing' event, an error, or the watchdog arrives, and the user cannot tell buffering from playing.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/audio/_audio/useTransport.ts:89 Button state comes from the request, not the machine, and there is no buffering or stalled state. Partly realized: a play watchdog is armed at line 91, superseded rejections are filtered by `gen`, and refusals are reported in words.
app/(studio)/audio/_audio/useTransport.ts:107 Engine-driven position is read on demand from the element. No playhead is held in reactive state, and only the human-speed `playing` id is.

app/(studio)/audio/_audio/useTransport.ts:66 One element is shared by the whole board. On unmount it clears the watchdog, removes its listeners, pauses, and strips and reloads the source, so no audio outlives the surface.
app/(studio)/audio/_audio/useTransport.ts:39 There is one playback engine, the HTMLAudioElement. The engine registry in arrangeRead is vendor makers, not playback engines.

app/(studio)/audio/_audio/useTransport.ts:53 Auditions are one take per press with no continuous run to keep alive. A failure is surfaced verbatim to the operator rather than recovered through a fallback.
app/(studio)/audio/_audio/Arrange.tsx:4 'Arrange' lays out workflow stages and groups, not a time-composed sequence.
app/(studio)/audio/_audio/AudioLane.tsx:168 Takes are finished files played from a stored src, not produced ahead of the playhead.
